scope: Pinned EP<=8 training wrapper implemented; eight CPU stub/autograd cases passed with no NPU/PG/UDMA initialization. EP16 isolated source patch prepared and CPU checked, not device-supported yet.
forward: Original APIs consume BF16 weight[E,K,N]; convert canonical train W1[E,2I,H] and W2[E,H,I] with transpose(-1,-2).contiguous() each fresh training step unless an explicitly versioned update cache is separately measured.
Pack by global expert; alltoallv_gmm(...output_all_to_allv=True) gives GU and exact Xe ordered local expert/source rank.
Preserve BF16 GU, FP32 SwiGLU then BF16 A; gmm_alltoallv returns unweighted source-packed Z. Save Z before source-side FP32 gate and BF16 per-contribution cast/reduction.
backward: dP per source route comes from dy and saved unweighted packed Z, no divide by p; zero-gate dP remains defined.
Pack weighted BF16 dY per route; alltoallv_gmm with canonical W2[E,H,I] as [E,K,N] produces dA. Export exact expert dZ for FP32 CATLASS dW2.
Compute BF16 dGU using saved BF16 GU/dA. FP32 CATLASS dW1=dGU^T Xe.
gmm_alltoallv(dGU,canonical W1[E,2I,H]) returns source-packed dX. Unpack/sum without applying gate again.
This is an explicit custom autograd adapter; original frozen EP8 module remains an operator-only baseline.

source_contracts.layout: local route length E; global received table source-rank/local-expert; host routes cause H2D metadata copies, device routes fallback behavior must be counted consistently
source_contracts.exclusive_runtime: init_udma_group tests core.runtime_busy and owns one process-local session. Do not keep an ElasticBuffer and ep_gmm UDMA group alive concurrently or assume two differently built deep_ep._C modules can share one Python import name.

comparison_protocol: Pinned EP8 wheel and adapted EP16 wheel isolated from frozen P0 native environment.

Use separate processes in controlled alternating trial order when comparing wheels/session owners; same route/input/weight seed and exact shape/dtype/casts/export cost, lifecycle creation before warmup and outside measured operator/full-step scope.
EP8 uses its own same-EP P0/CANN controls; no direct speedup claim comparing EP8 to EP16.
